headline: Texas Overwhelms USC in Dominant Ground Display
body: Texas put on a clinic in power football on Saturday, dismantling USC 41-11 behind a relentless ground attack that accumulated 376 rushing yards. The Longhorns controlled the line of scrimmage from the opening drive and never relinquished it, forcing USC into a perpetual deficit that left the Trojans unable to establish any rhythm on either side of the ball.

Arch Manning orchestrated the offense with surgical precision, completing 22 of 35 passes for 237 yards and five touchdowns. But the real story belonged to the running game. Texas's rushing attack was so suffocating that USC's defense had no choice but to stack the box, yet still couldn't slow the onslaught. The Trojans' porous run defense allowed chunks of yardage on nearly every carry, and by the third quarter, the game had devolved into garbage time.

USC's quarterback Moss struggled mightily, completing just 10 of 27 attempts for 135 yards with no touchdowns. The Trojans gained only 136 total yards—fewer than Texas accumulated on the ground alone—and never threatened to score after falling behind early. Texas's defensive coordinator sent consistent pressure that rattled Moss, with Lefau recording two sacks as part of a stifling effort that kept USC perpetually on its heels.
turningPoint: Texas's Wisner broke loose for 171 rushing yards, and by midway through the second quarter it became clear USC's defense had no answer, allowing the Longhorns to establish a comfortable margin that made the outcome inevitable.

unsungHero.name: Lefau
unsungHero.why: While Manning earns Player of the Game honors for his passing touchdowns, Lefau's two sacks and five tackles were the foundation that allowed Texas's offense to dictate pace and rhythm without USC ever generating offensive momentum.
